metadata.note: All prices reflect on-demand pricing in primary US region. Reserved instances offer 29-53% savings.

t3_medium.use_case: General purpose, web app servers, light workloads

g4dn_xlarge.specs: 4 vCPU, 16 GiB memory, 1x NVIDIA T4 GPU
g4dn_xlarge.use_case: GPU-accelerated LLM inference, ML training, video processing

backups.automated_backups: Free up to 100% of provisioned size

pricing.multi_az_impact: Doubles compute and storage costs (e.g., $129.94 → $259.88/mo for db.m5.large)

deployment.estimated_first_deploy: < 1 hour for basic setup via console or Terraform
deployment.scaling_approach: Vertical (instance type change, brief downtime) or Read Replicas for horizontal

managed_rds_cons: Data transfer costs between EC2 and RDS across AZ
Backup storage not included in instance price
Cannot directly SSH into database host
self_managed_cons: High availability requires custom replication setup

scaling.approach: Vertical scaling for RDS (instance type change with brief downtime)
scaling.read_replicas: Available for read scaling, cross-region supported
scaling.autoscaling: RDS Autoscaling not available; manual scaling required

postgresql_capabilities.backup_restore: Automated daily snapshots, point-in-time recovery to any second
postgresql_capabilities.snapshot_export: Export snapshots to S3 for external processing

network_isolation.vpc_deployment: Launch RDS in custom VPC with security group rules
network_isolation.no_public_endpoint: Can disable public accessibility, force private subnet-only
network_isolation.vpc_peering: Supported for cross-VPC access without internet

gpu_support.ec2_gpu: Yes - g4dn.xlarge, g4dn.12xlarge for T4 GPUs; p3/p4 for training
gpu_support.rds_gpu: No GPU support in RDS; use EC2 for inference

managed_postgresql_general_purpose.note: Dedicated CPU tier; pricing similar to Basic tier at equivalent memory sizes

additional_costs.read_replica_note: Per replica per month; can span regions

included_features: Free intra-region bandwidth between Droplets and DB

pros: No hidden I/O or IOPS charges
cons: Storage can only increase, not decrease (requires migration)
Smaller instance size options vs AWS
Regional pricing not as aggressive as some competitors

scaling.approach: Vertical only (must migrate to larger cluster)
scaling.read_replicas: Available; billed at same rate as primary
scaling.failover: Standby HA option doubles cost (primary + standby)

postgresql_capabilities.backup_restore: Automated daily snapshots; point-in-time recovery included

network_isolation.private_connection: Droplets connect to DB over private network, no internet exposure needed

typical_monthly_cost.with_ha: Droplet $24 + DB Primary $122.10 + DB Standby $122.10 ≈ $268/month (no app GPU support)

gcp_cloud_run.name: GCP Cloud Run (Serverless) + Cloud SQL PostgreSQL

cloud_run_request_based_billing.note: Pricing varies by region; other regions may cost 10-25% more

cloud_run_monthly_example_small.assumptions: 100,000 requests/month, 1 vCPU allocated, 512 MiB memory, avg request duration 1 second
cloud_run_monthly_example_small.note: Under free tier, actual cost would be $0

cloud_run_monthly_example_medium.assumptions: 1M requests/month, 2 vCPU, 2 GiB memory, avg request duration 2 seconds
cloud_run_monthly_example_medium.note: Does not include free tier reduction

cloud_sql_high_availability.note: Doubles vCPU and memory charges for standby instance

example_db_n1_standard_4_ha.storage_increase: Slight increase depending on replica location

data_transfer.internet_egress: First 1 GB/month free, then $0.12/GB (varies by region)

deployment.scaling: Automatic - scales from 0 to thousands based on requests

cloud_run_pros: Fully serverless - pay only for execution time
Automatic scaling, from zero to thousands
No cold start charges (only latency impact)
cloud_run_cons: Cold starts introduce latency (not billed but impacts UX)
cloud_sql_cons: More expensive than self-managed for sustained traffic
IP allowlisting less flexible than VPC

scaling.cloud_run: Automatic horizontal scaling based on request concurrency
scaling.cloud_sql: Vertical scaling only; requires instance type change
scaling.read_replicas: Available in Cloud SQL; different pricing tier

postgresql_capabilities.backup_restore: Automated daily backups; point-in-time recovery available
postgresql_capabilities.export: Export to Cloud Storage or BigQuery

network_isolation.cloud_run: Global endpoint (public); no direct VPC integration (Cloud Run 2nd gen supports VPC connectors)
network_isolation.cloud_sql: IP allowlist or VPC service peering for private access
network_isolation.vpc_connector: Cloud Run 2nd gen can use VPC Connector for private Cloud SQL access

gpu_support.alternative_for_gpu: Use Compute Engine (GCE) or Google Cloud's Vertex AI for GPU workloads

typical_monthly_cost.small_app: Cloud Run ~$5-10 (under free tier) + Cloud SQL db.f1.micro ($8) + storage ($2) ≈ $15-20/month
typical_monthly_cost.medium_app: Cloud Run $50-100 + Cloud SQL db.n1.standard.2 ($78) + storage ($10) ≈ $138-188/month
typical_monthly_cost.note: Very cost-effective for bursty/intermittent workloads; breaks even with VMs around 30-40% sustained utilization

pricing.note: Only hardware electricity and maintenance; no cloud fees

pros: No cold starts, no request latency penalties
Data stays on your servers (compliance advantage)
cons: No automatic failover without custom setup

networking: Do NOT expose database port to the internet
Use internal Docker network for app ↔ DB communication
Use reverse proxy (nginx/Traefik) for external ingress only
secrets_management: Use .env files (gitignored) or external secrets manager
Docker Compose 1.40+: secrets support for mounted files
Avoid hardcoding passwords in compose files
health_checks: Define healthcheck policy for all services
App healthcheck: HTTP liveness probe endpoint
profiles_and_environments: Use Docker Compose profiles for conditional services
Separate compose files: docker-compose.prod.yml with different resource limits
data_persistence: Volumes survive container restart, upgrade, or accidental rm
backups: Script daily pg_dump to persistent storage
Use cron inside sidecar container or host cron
Store backups on separate disk/NAS for redundancy
Test restore regularly (backup is not backup without restore)
resource_limits: Set memory limits to prevent runaway containers
CPU limits/shares to prevent single service monopolizing
PostgreSQL max_connections tuned to memory available
logging: Aggregate logs to stdout (Docker captures for inspection)
Use log drivers (json-file, syslog) for rotation
Limit log file size to prevent disk exhaustion
docker_files: Multi-stage Dockerfile to keep image size small
Use specific version tags, not latest

postgresql_capabilities.backup_restore: pg_dump (logical backup) or pg_basebackup (physical), user-managed script
postgresql_capabilities.on_disk_storage: Full control; can use raw partitions, NAS, or cloud storage mounts

network_isolation.default: Docker network isolation by default (containers invisible to internet)
network_isolation.custom_networks: Create overlay networks for multi-host setups
network_isolation.firewall_rules: Host OS firewall (ufw, firewalld) controls external access

gpu_support.compose_gpu: Docker Compose 1.40+ supports runtime: nvidia for GPU containers
gpu_support.use_case: LLM inference on local GPU (e.g., RTX 3090, A100)

scaling.approach: Vertical only (upgrade hardware) or horizontal with docker-compose scale (stateless app only)

typical_monthly_cost.hardware_only_example: Server purchase $2000 amortized over 48 months = $41/mo (plus electricity ~$30-50/mo, maintenance)
typical_monthly_cost.vs_cloud: Competitive with cloud at >$100/month sustained usage; cheaper for bursty workloads if hardware already owned

auto_scaling.aws_ec2_rds: Partial (RDS: vertical only; EC2: horizontal with ALB)

vendor_lock_in_risk.digitalocean: Medium (standard PostgreSQL, moderate costs to migrate)
vendor_lock_in_risk.gcp_cloud_run: Medium (Cloud Run specific; Cloud SQL is standard PostgreSQL)

ops_burden.aws_ec2_rds: Low (AWS handles RDS; you manage EC2)
ops_burden.digitalocean: Low (fully managed DB; simple droplet management)
ops_burden.gcp_cloud_run: Very low (Cloud Run fully managed; Cloud SQL mostly managed)
ops_burden.docker_compose_local: Very high (backup, patching, failover all manual)

startup_mvp.reason: Free tier covers initial load; pay-as-you-grow; minimal ops burden; easy to migrate later

production_small_team.reason: Transparent pricing, no hidden costs, solid managed DB, user-friendly dashboard

production_large_scale.reason: Widest instance options, best for GPU-accelerated workloads, mature ecosystem

compliance_data_residency.recommended: Docker Compose (self-hosted) or AWS with dedicated hardware
compliance_data_residency.reason: Full control over data location; Docker for on-prem, AWS Dedicated Instances for compliance

llm_inference_with_gpu.recommended: AWS EC2 g4dn.xlarge or Docker Compose with local GPU
llm_inference_with_gpu.reason: AWS: best GPU variety and cost; Docker: cheapest if hardware already owned

burstable_workloads.reason: Scale to zero cost; serverless pricing ideal for intermittent traffic

aws: Data transfer between EC2 and RDS across AZ ($0.01/GB)
RDS backup storage beyond 100% of instance size ($0.095/GiB-month)
Elastic IP charges if static IP not in use
digitalocean: Storage overages billed in 10 GiB increments (not linear)
Storage can only grow, not shrink (forces migration to reduce)
gcp: Internet egress ($0.12/GB after 1GB free) scales per region
Cloud SQL High Availability doubles compute without warning
Cloud Run custom domains don't have separate charges but Cloud CDN does
docker_compose: Unplanned downtime costs (no SLA, no failover)
